records.name: Team Foster
records.summary: A nonprofit that raises money for trained service dogs for injured veterans, and supports each veteran and dog team after the dog arrives. Its office is in Conshohocken, Montgomery County.
records.notes: Out of area: the office is in Conshohocken and the site names no Philadelphia event. The IRS record uses a Philadelphia PO Box (19103). The site has no dated items. records.notes: A school, not a community group. The only public way in is an admissions application for students. records.name: Casino Free Philadelphia
records.summary: A volunteer coalition that has pushed to keep casinos out of Philadelphia since the mid 2000s. The newest coverage we found is from 2014, so check whether it is still active before you go.
records.what_you_do: Past work included public meetings, protests and direct action against casino plans. We could not confirm what the group does now.

first_step.how: Read recent Philadelphia news about casino proposals to see whether the group is still active before reaching out.
first_step.basis: No current contact for the group could be confirmed.

records.notes: The group's own domain, casinofreephilly.org, now shows an online gambling promotion that has nothing to do with the group. Do not link it. No working contact page was found, so no contacts are recorded. The newest dated item found is the 2014 article. Older coverage in search results (from 2006 to 2009) is not counted as a sign of life. Search budget was used up before a current contact could be found. Owner decision: keep as dormant or hide.

records.name: Coalition of Labor Union Women, Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a national group of union women that has worked on pay equity, paid sick leave and health care. We could not confirm meetings or events in recent years.
records.what_you_do: Members have taken part in union and community advocacy on women's and workers' issues. Ask the national group whether the Philadelphia chapter still meets.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page on cluw.org to ask whether the Philadelphia chapter still holds meetings.
first_step.basis: The national site says to contact the organization through its Contact Us or Local Chapters pages, and it lists no local meeting times.

records.notes: The newest dated chapter evidence is the Temple University Special Collections finding aid for the chapter's records (SCRC 692). It covers board records for 2019 to 2022, and the records were donated in 2022. Nothing from 2023 to 2026 about the chapter was found. The national site (dated 2026) lists no Philadelphia chapter and no local meeting. The contact link in the website field is the national site, not the chapter. The IRS record lists 22 S 22nd St. An undated Bryn Mawr page gives a chapter president and phone number; not used because it is undated. The search budget was spent on this group.

records.name: Crescent Boat Club
records.summary: A member-run rowing club on the Schuylkill River at Boathouse Row. Adults can join and row at any level, and young people can take part in summer and junior rowing programs.
records.what_you_do: Members row the club's boats on the river, from a first outing up to masters racing. The club also runs junior and summer rowing programs. Anyone can walk the public riverfront path, which is open year round.

schedule.text: Membership runs year round, with summer coaching and junior programs

cost.text: Membership dues apply. Amounts were not read.

first_step.how: Send an inquiry through the membership form on crescentboatclub.org, or apply to a summer or junior rowing program from the youth rowing page.
first_step.basis: The club says no rowing experience is needed and points newcomers to a membership inquiry form and beginner-friendly youth and summer programs.

records.notes: The IRS legal name is Crescent Foundation, at the same address as the club. Treated as the club, but the link is not verified. Newest dated post: 2025 Summer Rowing Programs, May 16, 2025. Membership page and dues amounts were not read. The club's site says to give 842 Kelly Drive, not #5, when calling 911 or 311. Two school and university crews also row from the boathouse; they were dropped from leads (see leads_only).

records.name: Delta Phi Epsilon
records.summary: A national social sorority based in Philadelphia, with college chapters and alumnae groups. Its educational foundation gives scholarships each year.
records.what_you_do: College members join a chapter and take part in its meetings, service and fundraising. Alumnae join local alumnae groups. The national group holds an International Leadership Forum every other summer and runs online social justice events.

first_step.how: Read the How To Join page on dphie.org, then email info@dphie.org to ask which chapter or alumnae group is near you.
first_step.basis: Students join by recruitment and alumnae by initiation. The site does not explain the steps, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Dated 2026 items on the national site: installation of the 2026 International Governing Board, the 2026 to 2028 board slate, and 2026 scholarship recipients. The month of each item is not shown, so no last_sign_of_life is recorded. Chapter membership is not open to walk-ins. Owner decision: whether a sorority belongs in the directory. The two chapter records below are listed as duplicates of this record.

notes: All 15 batch groups were attempted. Verdicts: 10 publish, 1 hide, 1 not_a_group, 1 out_of_area, 2 duplicate. Searches: both used (cap is 2): one for Casino Free Philadelphia, one for the Philadelphia CLUW chapter. Fetches: 24 used of 60, budget not exhausted. Dead or taken over domains: cat-baret.com, childfamilyconnections.org and philadelphia2019.com do not resolve. casinofreephilly.org now shows an online gambling promotion, and delawarevalleysmartgrowth.org now shows an unrelated Vietnamese language blog with betting links. Do not link either taken over domain. Six publish records (Cat-Baret, Center for Creative Activities, Child and Family Connections, Corporate Responsibility Association, Dance for Independence, Delaware Valley Smart Growth Alliance) have no sources and unknown status. They should be held back until someone finds a working site. 404s on cluw.org/local-chapters and cluw.org/contact-us were not used; the Local Chapters link was not found. Owner decisions: OIC-CADI is hidden as a private school; the national sorority is published with invite-only entry and its two chapters are duplicates; Casino Free and CLUW are published as dormant with low confidence. Dropped from leads: Thomas Jefferson University women's rowing and Harriton High School Crew, which row from Crescent's boathouse. They are school and university teams, not community groups.
